new_jobs.description:
About Hilbert

Hilbert is a scalable, data science-first growth engine that gives B2C teams predictive clarity into user behavior, revenue drivers, and the actions that drive sustainable growth. Fully agentic by design, Hilbert shrinks months-long decision cycles to minutes.

From Fortune 10 enterprises to beloved brands like FreshDirect, Blank Street, and Levain Bakery, operators run their growth on Hilbert. We're also co-building alongside leading AI companies.

The Mission: Turn Ground Truth Into Growth

Hilbert has two parts: a data foundation that gives our AI agents a high-fidelity view of each business, and an agentic web app where growth teams find and act on insights. The scores and audiences you build feed both: our agents reason with them, and our activation sends them into paid media and CRM.

The hard problem

Every customer's data is different, their compute may be ClickHouse, Databricks, Snowflake or BigQuery, and their teams want proof, not promises. Your models have to work in that environment and show measured uplift. We want every pod to stay lean and efficient across very different customer environments, delivering quality work at startup speed. You focus on delivery; our sales engineers handle pre-sales. Your work centers on customers in your own region: supporting customers elsewhere is a rare exception, and your global work is mainly staying aligned with Hilbert colleagues in other regions.

What You'll Do

Feature stores: build customer-specific, point-in-time correct features on the data foundation.
Models: train, tune and validate propensity, churn, lifetime value, uplift and custom models, starting from our ML templates and building custom models when a customer needs something the templates don't cover. New model types that many customers will need are built first by our product engineering team, and you roll them out to later customers.
Model analysis: go beyond aggregate metrics to verify what each model has learned, what drives its scores, and how it behaves across segments and on edge cases.
Deployment: models run in the customer's own environment or on our managed stack. In either case, understand the constraints, pin down the requirements, design the ML system to fit, and write the scores and audiences our agents and activation use.
Measurement: own the statistical design inside our growth team's measurement plan, from power and holdout setup to uplift analysis.
Trust: document models for the customer's data science and risk teams, then monitor and retrain them in production.
Productization: turn repeated features and model patterns into product with our product engineering team.

What Success Looks Like

Audiences built from your models lift the agreed growth metric, such as conversion or retention, against a holdout group, and that result decides whether the customer takes them to production.

Who You Are

The translator: you explain a model to a customer's data science team and earn their trust.
The experimenter: you'd rather prove uplift in a holdout test than show off an offline metric.
The pilot: you get the most out of AI agents across model iterations, from feature ideas and experiment runs to error analysis, and help build them into how the team works.
The systems thinker: you build reusable features, pipelines and automation instead of one-off models, so a small team can deliver across very different environments.
Extensive applied ML experience on tabular customer data, with strong Python and ML libraries.
Extensive hands-on deep learning experience, from designing architectures and loss functions to training and shipping models in production, with PyTorch or a similar framework.
Feature engineering in SQL warehouses such as Databricks, Snowflake or BigQuery.
Working data engineering experience: building and debugging pipelines, data orchestration, data modeling and data quality checks, enough to own your feature pipelines end to end with our data engineers.
Production ML with tools such as MLflow, Weights & Biases or Vertex AI.
Solid experiment design and uplift measurement.
Comfortable working in a distributed team across time zones.
Fluent Spanish for roles based in Latin America.

Nice to have

DevOps, software architecture and security knowledge
Growth-focused data projects experience
Industry experience such as e-commerce, retail, fintech, telco and media
Model governance in regulated industries such as banking and telco: model documentation, explainability and PII handling
Able to travel to the US when necessary

Reporting and location

You report to your pod's Lead Delivery Engineer and work alongside our data delivery engineers and product engineering team. The role is based in Americas. Delivery runs remotely, with occasional visits to our largest customers.

Why join us

At Hilbert, we move fast, work collaboratively, and give people real ownership over their impact. As a fast-growing company, there's no shortage of room to grow — you'll take on new challenges quickly and shape the path as you go.

new_jobs.description:
Description

Prime Video is a first-stop entertainment destination offering customers a vast collection of premium programming in one app available across thousands of devices. Prime members can customize their viewing experience and find their favorite movies, series, documentaries, and live sports – including Amazon MGM Studios-produced series and movies; licensed fan favorites; and programming from Prime Video subscriptions such as Apple TV+, HBO Max, Peacock, Crunchyroll and MGM+. All customers, regardless of whether they have a Prime membership or not, can rent or buy titles via the Prime Video Store, and can enjoy even more content for free with ads.

Are you interested in shaping the future of entertainment? Prime Video's technology teams are creating best-in-class digital video experience.

As a Prime Video team member, you’ll have end-to-end ownership of the product, user experience, design, and technology required to deliver state-of-the-art experiences for our customers. You’ll get to work on projects that are fast-paced, challenging, and varied. You’ll also be able to experiment with new possibilities, take risks, and collaborate with remarkable people.

We’ll look for you to bring your diverse perspectives, ideas, and skill-sets to make Prime Video even better for our customers. With global opportunities for talented technologists, you can decide where a career Prime Video Tech takes you!

Key job responsibilities

The Science Challenges Include

Heterogeneous customer responses. The same customer responds differently to ads depending on what they’re watching, how engaged they are, and their broader streaming context. We need to understand and predict this variation to make better advertising decisions in real time.
Signal sparsity in streaming. Unlike search or retail advertising, streaming offers no clicks, no conversions, and limited direct feedback. We must develop creative approaches to infer customer preferences, intent, and tolerance from indirect behavioral signals.
Personalization at scale. A one-size-fits-all ad experience leaves value on the table for both customers and the business. We build systems that adapt ad load, placement, and content to individual viewers across 100M+ customers and 100k+ titles.
Small effects, large variance. Ad interventions typically produce 0.1-2% shifts in engagement, effects easily overwhelmed by natural behavioral variance. Measuring, attributing, and optimizing these small signals requires rigorous experimental design and causal methodologies.
Competing objectives. Revenue, customer engagement, long-term retention, and advertiser value are in tension. We develop principled frameworks to navigate these tradeoffs and optimize for sustainable outcomes rather than any single metric.

A day in the life

Contribute to the research and development of ML models that personalize advertising decisions for 100M+ customers across 100k+ titles, with production deployment in mind
Develop deep learning architectures (multi-task learning, embedding-based representations) for customer behavior prediction at scale
Design and analyze large-scale A/B experiments, applying causal inference techniques to measure and optimize the impact of ad strategies on customer engagement and monetization
Partner with engineering to ensure models meet production latency and scalability requirements
Collaborate with product managers to frame business problems as tractable ML problems and translate findings into product decisions
Shape the team’s scientific roadmap, identifying high-impact research directions

About The Team

Prime Video Ads is pioneering the use of Generative AI, Deep Learning and Causal ML to empower the next generation of Ads experience in Prime Video. Our vision is to build the world’s most valuable and differentiated ad-supported streaming platform: one where every ad is relevant to the viewer, and every dollar spent by an advertiser delivers measurable results. We are seeking lead applied scientists who have demonstrated experience in advancing state of the art ML algorithms, particularly in Personalization, Relevance, Casual Inference and Gen-AI areas. Your role will be to deliver these innovations as production-ready systems at Amazon scale.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of building models for business application experience
PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of CS, CE, ML or related field experience
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building machine learning models or developing algorithms for business application
Experience in solving business problems through machine learning, data mining and statistical algorithms
Experience with programming languages such as Python, Java, C++

new_jobs.title: Robotics AI Engineer - Robot Learning
new_jobs.description:
Help us teach robots to do things they've never done before.

Janicki Industries | Sedro-Woolley, Washington | Full-Time

Onsite, Hybrid and Remote opportunities available | $120,000-$220,000 annually

We're building robots that learn from people, practice in simulation, and develop the ability to perform useful work in the real world.

At Janicki Industries, we've spent more than 30 years solving difficult engineering problems and building advanced hardware for aerospace, defense, and space programs. Now we're bringing that experience to one of the most exciting challenges in engineering: creating intelligent robots that can adapt to new tasks and work in environments that were never designed for automation.

And we have some extraordinary opportunities to put that technology to work.

A Different Kind of Factory

Janicki has committed to building an $800 million advanced manufacturing facility in Montana to produce precision metallic components for the aerospace and defense industries. Ground has already been broken on the first building.

We're designing the facility around a high level of automation. The first phase is expected to include dozens of five-axes milling machines, automated warehouses, robotic material loading, automated coordinate measuring machines, and automated metal finishing and coating systems. Massive robotic vehicles will move pallets weighing as much as 40,000 pounds throughout the factory.

But what makes this project particularly interesting isn't just the scale.

Most factory automation is designed to do the same thing, over and over, at high speed. Our challenges are different. We manufacture highly complex parts in relatively small quantities, often with significant differences from one job to the next.

This is high-mix, low-volume manufacturing, and it presents an entirely different set of robotics problems.

We need robots that can recognize unfamiliar parts, understand changing environments, adapt to different tasks, and work alongside sophisticated manufacturing equipment. Many of the capabilities we want simply don't exist as ready-made solutions.

We see enormous potential in combining modern AI, computer vision, robot learning, and simulation to solve these problems. Our goal is to make this one of the most advanced and flexible manufacturing facilities in the world.

You'll have an opportunity to help develop the technology that makes it possible.

Teaching Robots to Learn

Our robotics team is exploring a new approach to automation: rather than programming every movement, we want to teach robots through human demonstrations, train neural networks to reproduce those behaviors, and use simulation to help them learn and improve.

We're interested in the rapidly developing world of vision-language-action models, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and robotic foundation models such as NVIDIA Isaac GR00T.

We're also developing robots for applications outside traditional manufacturing. One of our first projects is an autonomous robot that cleans horse stalls using cameras, a robotic arm, and specialized tools. It's a deceptively difficult problem involving visual perception, object manipulation, and decision-making in an unpredictable environment.

These projects share an important goal: creating robots that can perform useful physical work without having every action programmed in advance.

We've assembled a team of mechanical, electrical, and software engineers and are looking for an AI engineer who wants to help develop the intelligence behind these machines.

What You'll Do

You'll work on the technologies that allow robots to learn new skills and apply them to physical tasks.

Robot Learning: Develop and train neural networks that translate visual information and human demonstrations into robotic actions. Work with imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and modern robot foundation models.
Vision-Language-Action Models: Build training pipelines using camera data and human teleoperation. Explore and adapt VLA approaches, including NVIDIA Isaac GR00T, to teach robots new manipulation skills.
Simulation: Use NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, and Omniverse to create realistic environments, generate training data, and train and evaluate robotic behaviors before deploying them to physical hardware.
Computer Vision: Develop perception systems that allow robots to recognize objects, understand their surroundings, and make decisions based on visual information. Apply technologies such as YOLO, image segmentation, and depth sensing.
Real-World Deployment: Work alongside our robotics, mechanical, and electrical engineers to bring trained models onto actual machines, evaluate their performance, and continually improve their capabilities.

You'll help shape our technical approach, select the tools and models we use, and determine how emerging AI technologies can be applied to real manufacturing and automation problems.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for an exceptionally capable engineer who enjoys difficult problems, learns quickly, and takes pride in making things work.

You'll Bring a Strong Foundation In Machine Learning, Software Engineering, Or Robotics, Along With Meaningful Hands-on Experience In At Least One Of These Areas

Robotics simulation and learning environments, particularly NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Omniverse, or similar platforms.
Training neural networks for robotic manipulation, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, or learning from human demonstrations.
Computer vision and perception, including object detection, segmentation, and models such as YOLO.
Developing and training AI models using Python, PyTorch, or comparable frameworks.

We're especially interested in engineers who have worked with vision-language-action models, teleoperation-based training, NVIDIA Isaac GR00T, or robotic systems that learn through experience.

A strong academic background in computer science, robotics, AI, or a related engineering discipline is valuable. We appreciate the preparation that comes from demanding university programs and excellent research environments. We're equally interested in people who have demonstrated exceptional ability by building and delivering impressive systems.

What matters most is your technical ability, your accomplishments, and the way you approach challenging engineering problems.

You don't need experience with every technology listed here.
If you've done outstanding work in one of these areas and are excited to expand into the others, we'd like to meet you.

2+ years of relevant engineering experience spanning robotics and AI. (Preferred)

Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or closely related field from an ABET-accredited. (Required)

Why Janicki?

There aren't many places where you can develop advanced AI algorithms and work directly with the people who design, machine, assemble, and test the hardware those algorithms control.

Janicki is one of them.

We're a privately owned engineering and manufacturing company with decades of experience tackling ambitious projects in aerospace, defense, space, and advanced manufacturing. We have substantial engineering resources, sophisticated manufacturing facilities, and people who know how to turn difficult ideas into working technology.

Our robotics team is bringing together those capabilities with some of the most exciting developments in artificial intelligence.

You'll join a growing engineering group where your contributions can have a direct influence on the technology. You'll have the freedom to explore new approaches, the resources to test them on physical hardware, and the opportunity to see your work become part of real machines and manufacturing systems.

The Montana facility gives us a remarkable opportunity to develop intelligent automation on a scale that few robotics teams get to experience.

We're not looking simply to automate the way factories have always operated. We're interested in what becomes possible when robots can learn, adapt, and take on tasks that previously required human judgment and flexibility.

If that sounds like an exciting engineering problem, we'd like to talk.

Work Where You Want to Live

Our headquarters is in Sedro-Woolley, Washington, in the beautiful Skagit Valley at the edge of the North Cascades.

For people who love the outdoors, this part of Western Washington is hard to beat. Hiking, mountain biking, skiing at Mount Baker, kayaking, fishing, and exploring the San Juan Islands are all within reach. Bellingham offers a lively university town with restaurants, music, and outdoor recreation, while Seattle provides the cultural and professional opportunities of a major technology center.

We'd love to find someone in the greater Seattle or Puget Sound area who can spend occasional time working with our team and physical hardware in Sedro-Woolley.

We're also open to hybrid and remote candidates, including engineers in the San Francisco Bay Area.
Monthly visits to our Washington facilities will help keep you connected to the team and the machines we're developing.

Compensation

The proposed annual base salary range is $120,000-$220,000
, plus a discretionary bonus, 401(k) matching, vacation, and health benefits. Depending on experience and qualifications, subject to final approval. The actual salary will vary by geographic region and job experience. We will share detailed compensation data for a specific location during the recruiting process

Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance with employer contribution
Disability insurance as well as Life/AD&D insurance
HSA (Health Savings Account) with employer contribution and FSA (Flexible Savings Account)
401k with employer matching

new_jobs.title: Scientist II, Applied Machine Learning
new_jobs.description:
A-Alpha Bio is an early-stage, rapidly growing biotechnology platform company headquartered in Seattle, WA. We are focused on building the foundational data layer for AI-driven protein engineering. We provide biopharma companies and model builders with access to ground truth experimental datasets, including affinity and structure, for training, benchmarking and validating AI protein models. In parallel, we apply our data and models directly with select partners to engineer next-generation dual-specific and molecular glue therapeutics, and to discover and optimize differentiated biologics.

A-Alpha Bio is headquartered in Seattle, WA, but remote applicants are welcome to apply. Candidates must reside in the United States.

Starting Salary Range:
$139,000 - $175,000 annually

Exemption Status:
Exempt

Location Expectations
: Remote-Eligible (expected travel to Seattle HQ once per quarter)

Reporting To
: Director, Applied Machine Learning

Role Description

A-Alpha Bio is seeking a Scientist II to join our Applied Machine Learning team in turning large-scale protein interaction data into insights and models that advance antibody and protein engineering. In this role, you’ll lead computational work for both internal research and external collaborations, from defining scientific questions and analysis plans to developing models and communicating results. Working with AlphaSeq datasets, you’ll connect experimental measurements with protein sequence and structural information to understand binding, evaluate computational design methods, and guide future experiments. Success in this role will depend on ability to state assumptions, clearly define goals and objectives, and explain your procedures thoughtfully.

Key Responsibilities

Lead scientific analyses:Define and execute analysis plans for large-scale protein interaction datasets (often 1M PPIs), including evaluating binding affinity, specificity, and the performance of antibody and protein design methods.
Develop and evaluate ML models: Build, train, and apply models using experimental measurements, protein sequences, and structural information. Design rigorous benchmarks and assess model performance, uncertainty, and generalization.
Connect computation with experiments: Collaborate with experimental scientists to shape study designs, interpret results, investigate unexpected findings, and recommend follow-up experiments.
Deliver results to external partners: Serve as the computational lead for assigned projects, producing clear presentations, reports, and well-documented datasets for both internal teams and external collaborators. Many projects may have open-source elements, requiring a strong eye for detail and narrative.
Build reusable methods: Translate project-specific work into reliable analytical tools and workflows. Contribute maintainable Python code, review contributions, and document methods so others can use them.
Advance our scientific capabilities: Identify and develop new computational approaches that increase the value of AlphaSeq data for protein engineering.

Required

Qualifications & Experience

PhD in a relevant field with 2+ years of experience working on large-scale data analysis using biological sequence or structure data; or a bachelor’s degree with 10+ years of relevant experience, including 5+ years working onlarge-scale data analysis using biological sequence or structure data; or an equivalent education and experience.
Demonstrated expertise in Python for scientific computing, data analysis, visualization, and ML model development.
Experience analyzing large experimental datasets and making scientifically defensible decisions about data quality, statistical methods, and interpretation.
Strong understanding of model evaluation, including appropriate baselines, data leakage, and the limits of conclusions drawn from a benchmark.
Ability to translate an open-ended scientific question into an executable plan and deliver reproducible results with limited supervision.
Clear communication skills, including the ability to explain methods, findings, and limitations to computational and experimental audiences.
Experience contributing to a shared codebase through version control, code review, and documentation.

Preferred

Experience with antibody or protein engineering, particularly the relationship between sequence, structure, and binding.
Familiarity with the structural modeling of protein complexes and evaluation of structure prediction or generative design methods.
Use of modern ML frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Hugging Face.
Experience processing and analyzing next-generation sequencing data, (Illumina, Oxford Nanopore, etc.).
Experience developing analytical tools or workflows used by other scientists.

In 2018, A-Alpha Bio spun out of the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design and Center for Synthetic Biology – both communities filled with brilliant and highly entrepreneurial scientists. Since the company’s inception, we have built and scaled AlphaSeq, our high-throughput platform for quantitatively measuring protein-protein interactions at unprecedented scale. What began as a technology for generating large, standardized affinity datasets has grown into a broader data engine for AI-driven protein engineering. New members of the team should expect a fast-paced, highly dynamic, and interdisciplinary work environment. We are building a diverse, meritocratic, and supportive team that shares our values of speaking the truth, shooting for the moon, taking the reins, playing for the team, and improving the world.

A-Alpha Bio is headquartered in a custom designed lab and office space in downtown Seattle’s Belltown neighborhood. We are fortunate to be situated in a region that is renowned for its premier outdoor activities, including hiking, biking, climbing, skiing, kayaking, sailing, and more. At A-Alpha, you’ll find many who love the outdoors, but also gamers, amateur chefs, explorers, sports fans, bakers, crafters, photographers, brewers, jetsetters, animal lovers, and artists. Whatever your passions, you belong at A-Alpha Bio!

new_jobs.title: Senior Associate, Azure AI Engineer
new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

As a Senior Associate - Azure AI Engineer you will design and develop generative AI solutions for clients within our Advisory practice, applying Azure-based engineering to application development and modernization. In this role, you will shape AI architectures from analytical modeling and prompt engineering through testing, deployment, and maintenance. Using Python, Azure AI Services, and large language model APIs, you will build applications that use retrieval-augmented generation and vector databases to ground responses in client data. You will also develop agent workflows with LangGraph, coordinating models, tools, and application components to address business challenges.

As a Senior Associate, you will own assigned workstreams and deliverables, using critical thinking when technical choices or client requirements are unclear. You will build meaningful client connections by listening to different perspectives, anticipating needs, and explaining tradeoffs in the context of broader business goals. Guiding junior colleagues and reviewing their work will help you develop your approach to managing others while maintaining professional and technical standards. Through feedback and reflection, you will deepen your technical skills, adapt to changing project conditions, and build your professional reputation through dependable delivery.

Responsibilities

Designing Azure-based generative AI architectures and analytical models that turn client data into actionable insights and translate business needs into technical deliverables
Building conversational applications with Azure AI Services, Azure OpenAI Service, LLM APIs, prompt engineering, and context engineering to support client decision-making
Developing retrieval-augmented generation pipelines using data modeling, information retrieval systems, and vector databases to ground model responses in source data
Orchestrating AI agents with LangGraph, LangChain, and Model Context Protocol, coordinating tool access, shared state, and error handling across workflows
Creating cloud-native microservices in Python, C#, and JavaScript, integrating AI capabilities with existing applications through Azure API Management and enterprise service buses
Applying GitHub Copilot and Claude Code across development and testing, using DevOps and LLMOps practices to deploy and maintain solutions on Azure Kubernetes Service
Evaluating model outputs and application behavior through LLM evaluation, guardrails, and performance monitoring, while applying identity, access, and key management controls
Collaborating with clients and colleagues to clarify requirements, manage assigned workstreams, review deliverables, mentor junior team members, and incorporate feedback throughout the development life cycle

What You Must Have

At least a Bachelor's degree
At least 3 years of experience

What Sets You Apart

Building generative AI applications with Azure AI Services, Azure OpenAI Service, and LLM APIs for client projects
Orchestrating AI agent workflows with LangGraph and Model Context Protocol, including tool integration and error handling
Developing retrieval-augmented generation pipelines with vector databases and context engineering
Evaluating LLM outputs and applying guardrails during prompt engineering, testing, and application development
Deploying Python or C# microservices on Microsoft Azure using DevOps practices, Azure Kubernetes Service, and application monitoring
Guiding junior team members through technical reviews while communicating design tradeoffs and navigating changing client priorities

new_jobs.title: Associate Data Scientist, Personal Lines
new_jobs.description:
Assoc Data Scientist - GD08BE

We’re determined to make a difference and are proud to be an insurance company that goes well beyond coverages and policies. Working here means having every opportunity to achieve your goals – and to help others accomplish theirs, too. Join our team as we help shape the future.

The Hartford seeks an energetic and passionate Associate Data Scientist to build high-performing, empathetic analytics teams and deliver smarter product pricing decisions. This role will focus on the Auto line within the Personal Insurance Loss and Demand Modeling team. We support our product and pricing partners through the delivery of rigorously developed and tested solutions including models and implementation support.

In this role, you will contribute across the full model lifecycle, from data exploration and feature engineering through model development, validation, implementation, and monitoring. Generalized linear models are a core component of our work, alongside machine learning techniques such as gradient boosted trees and modern MLOps practices. You will also help improve the tools, workflows, and standards that enable the team to support a broad and evolving portfolio of models.

Responsibilities

Develop and evaluate predictive modeling solutions that support the personal auto class plan, unconstrained loss models, and customer demand models.
Evaluate new data sources and modeling approaches to boost product performance. Engineer features to uncover additional signal for our models.
Support model implementations with state Departments of Insurance (DOI), serving as a subject matter expert on the models you build and responding to DOI queries.
Maintain a portfolio of repositories and scripts and suggest improvements to workflows. Assist in the modernization of model deployments using our cloud-based MLOps tools.
Collaborate with team members to plan and deliver projects in an Agile framework.
Develop and maintain analytic packages to facilitate data collection, analysis, and modeling.
Stay up to date on machine learning techniques, apply them to your work, and share them with your team and the broader data science community.
Ensure analytic reproducibility, conduct code reviews, and maintain git hygiene.
Share results with partners and make recommendations based on outcomes.

This role will have a Hybrid work schedule, with the expectation of working in an office (Columbus, OH, Chicago, IL, Hartford, CT or Charlotte, NC) 3 days a week (Tuesday through Thursday).

Experiences & Skills

Master's degree in Statistics, Data Science, Mathematics, Actuarial Science, Economics, Engineering, Physics, or similar analytical field.
Experience in the insurance industry, particularly in loss cost modeling or personal insurance products, is a plus but not required. Candidates with relevant modeling experience from other industries are encouraged to apply.
Comfort with generalized linear models and related techniques (e.g., ridge and lasso regression, GAMs) and the math behind them.
Hands-on experience with Python and a track record of delivering clean, literate code in a reproducible environment.
Experience using GitHub for version control, documentation, code collaboration, and technical project management.
Able to independently research solutions, identify when you are stuck, and seek help when needed.
Strong interest in identifying and eliminating workflow inefficiencies. Passionate about tracking down the root cause of problems and identifying tradeoffs.
Demonstrated experience with listening to collaborators and brainstorming outcomes that address their business problems.
Experience building modeling solutions in cloud-native environments, such as SageMaker, a plus.
Committed to democratizing knowledge, evangelizing good practices, and supporting peers.

Candidate must be authorized to work in the US without company sponsorship. The company will not support the STEM OPT I-983 Training Plan endorsement for this position.

Compensation

The listed annualized base pay range is primarily based on analysis of similar positions in the external market. Actual base pay could vary and may be above or below the listed range based on factors including but not limited to performance, proficiency and demonstration of competencies required for the role. The base pay is just one component of The Hartford’s total compensation package for employees. Other rewards may include short-term or annual bonuses, long-term incentives, and on-the-spot recognition. The annualized base pay range for this role is:

$81,040 - $121,560

An Forward Deployment Engineer (FDE)
sits at the intersection of AI platform capabilities and business users — translating ambiguous business problems into working AI solutions, deploying them into the customer's environment, and iterating in tight loops until they deliver measurable value.

You will be the technical person closest to the client: sitting with platform owners and Enterprise Architects, understanding how their systems really work, and building agentic and GenAI proofs of concept that run on those systems. You are part engineer, part consultant, and part translator between business, architecture and delivery.

What You'll Do

Deliver end-to-end AI solutions
— Take a specific business problem from first conversation with the stakeholder through deployment, adoption and a measurable result, learning the existing systems, data flows, integrations and constraints along the way.
Embed with the client
— Work day-to-day with client’s platform owners and Enterprise Architects to map current-state platforms, data flows, integration points and constraints.
B uild in governance from day one
— Work with the GRC/compliance lead to apply data privacy, auditability, model risk and GxP-aware controls in everything you build.
Translate ambiguous, evolving business requirements into working software
— Turn fuzzy requirements into working software. Often there is no formal spec, so you work side by side with the people who own the problem and shape the solution with them.
Build vertical AI applications rapidly
— on top of the existing AI platform, using Snowflake Cortex, Databricks Genie, RAG pipelines and agentic workflows to solve narrow problems that carry high business value.
Prototype in days, not months
— Get a working Streamlit app, Databricks App or light web UI to business users within the first 1-2 weeks, then refine it from their real feedback.
Deploy solutions inside the customer's regulated environment
— respecting existing governance, RBAC, data residency, audit, and compliance constraints.
Instrument for measurement
— every deployed solution ships with usage metrics, adoption tracking, and business outcome telemetry from day one.
Own the "last mile" that makes AI actually usable
— data quirks, business rule exceptions, edge cases, user training, change management, and adoption support.
Work directly with business functions
— translating their language into technical solutions and back.
Build reusable patterns
— after solving a specific problem, extract the reusable pieces (prompts, retrieval patterns, UI components, evaluation harnesses) into shared assets other FDEs can leverage.
Accountable for the outcome, not just the code
– if the business user isn't getting value, the job isn't done regardless of the code being deployed.

Must-Have Technical Skills

Agentic and GenAI
— LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, Model Context Protocol (MCP), multi-agent patterns – with production usage, not tutorials
Evaluation and safety
— LLM evaluation frameworks, guardrails, red-teaming, prompt-injection defences
Full-stack AI application development
— End-to-end working system, with a UI, a backend and an LLM integration, in weeks rather than months
Python + FastAPI/Flask
for backend services, Streamlit / Databricks Apps / lightweight React
for user-facing interfaces
Direct hands-on with at least one of: Snowflake Cortex (Analyst/Search/Agents/LLM Functions) OR Databricks Genie (Genie Spaces, semantic models)
— you know these products well enough to configure, tune, and integrate them into vertical solutions
RAG pipeline construction
— chunking, embeddings, vector search (Pinecone, pgvector, Chroma, FAISS, Azure AI Search, Snowflake Cortex Search), retrieval evaluation, grounding, citation
Prompt engineering with evaluation discipline
— you know how to design prompts, evaluate them against ground truth, iterate based on hallucination and accuracy metrics
Cloud data platform fluency
— Snowflake and/or Databricks at working depth, plus at least one cloud provider (Azure preferred given the client environment, AWS/GCP acceptable) and it’s AIML services.
SQL and data modelling
— sufficient to work directly with governed datasets and semantic models
Git, CI/CD, and modern development workflows
— you own the deployment path, not just the local development
API design and integration
— you can integrate your solution into existing enterprise systems (SAP, Workday, Coupa, ERP, etc.) via REST APIs
Basic MLOps awareness
— you understand model versioning, prompt versioning, evaluation harnesses, observability (LangSmith, Datadog, Application Insights) — enough to hand off your solution to the MLOps team cleanly

Must-Have Non-Technical Skills

Direct customer/stakeholder communication
— you can sit in a room with a CFO office user, understand what's frustrating them, and translate that into a technical roadmap without needing a business analyst intermediary
Ambiguity tolerance
— you're comfortable starting work with a vague problem statement and refining it through prototypes rather than requiring detailed specs upfront
Product-shaped thinking
— you optimize for user adoption and business outcome, not for elegant architecture or full feature completeness
Speed-to-first-demo mindset
— you'd rather ship a rough working prototype in Week 1 than a polished spec in Week 4
Willingness to write throwaway code
— you know when to build for permanence and when to build for a demo; you don't over-engineer
Change management sensibility
— you understand that adoption requires more than good technology, and you're willing to do the user-training and hand-holding work to make solutions stick

Nice to Have

Pharma, life sciences, or CPG Finance domain experience
— familiarity with FP&A processes, financial consolidation, regulatory reporting, cost allocation, or clinical trial finance
Veeva CRM, IQVIA, SAP S/4HANA, SAP BW, Oracle Financials, Workday Adaptive
or similar enterprise Finance tooling
Regulated environment delivery
— SOX, GxP, data residency, audit trails
Snowflake Cortex certification, Databricks certification, or Azure AI Engineer Associate (AI-102)

Prior FDE, Solutions Engineer, Sales Engineer, or Field Engineer experience
at Palantir, Snowflake, Databricks, OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar
Startup / small-team experience
— you've had to wear multiple hats and ship end-to-end without organizational scaffolding
Direct experience with agentic workflows
(multi-agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop, tool-calling) in production, not just demos

Domain Skills — Finance Focus

Working understanding of Finance business processes
— order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, record-to-report, plan-to-report, close cycles, financial planning and analysis, management reporting, statutory reporting, tax reporting
Familiarity with common Finance data
— general ledger, cost centers, profit centers, chart of accounts, hierarchies, allocations, KPIs (revenue, gross margin, EBITDA, OPEX, working capital, DSO, DPO)
Ability to speak Finance's language
— variance analysis, forecasts vs actuals, budget vs actual, trend analysis, drill-through, drill-down, scenario planning
Comfort with governed enterprise data
— understanding why Finance data has to be trusted, auditable, and lineage-tracked, and why "just run an LLM on the raw data" is not an acceptable answer in a regulated environment

What We're NOT Looking For

Data Scientists
— this is not model training, fine-tuning, or ML research. The models are already there. This role is about applying them.
Pure Backend Engineers
— this role needs someone comfortable owning the full stack including the user-facing surface, not just APIs
Pure ML Engineers / MLOps Engineers
— those are separate roles. FDEs deploy AI value; MLOps operates AI infrastructure; DE engineers build the AI-ready data. Adjacent, not the same.
Architects who don't ship code
— this is a builder role. If your resume is 5 years of "architected" without "built," this is not your role.
Consulting-shaped engineers who need a full spec
— you'll be starting from ambiguous problem statements and iterating; if that scares you, this isn't the role.
AI Platform Engineers who don't want customer contact
— the customer conversation is a core part of the job, not a burden to be minimized.

At Capital One, we are creating responsible and reliable AI systems, changing banking for good. For years, Capital One has been an industry leader in using machine learning to create real-time, personalized customer experiences. Our investments in technology infrastructure and world-class talent — along with our deep experience in machine learning — position us to be at the forefront of enterprises leveraging AI. From informing customers about unusual charges to answering their questions in real time, our applications of AI & ML are bringing humanity and simplicity to banking. We are committed to continuing to build world-class applied science and engineering teams to deliver our industry leading capabilities with breakthrough product experiences and scalable, high-performance AI infrastructure. At Capital One, you will help bring the transformative power of emerging AI capabilities to reimagine how we serve our customers and businesses who have come to love the products and services we build.

Team Description:

The Intelligent Foundations and Experiences (IFX) team is at the center of bringing our vision for AI at Capital One to life. We work hand-in-hand with our partners across the company to advance the state of the art in science and AI engineering, and we build and deploy proprietary solutions that are central to our business and deliver value to millions of customers. Our AI models and platforms empower teams across Capital One to enhance their products with the transformative power of AI, in responsible and scalable ways for the highest leverage impact.

What You’ll Do:

Partner with a cross-functional team of engineers, research scientists, technical program managers, and product managers to deliver AI-powered products that change how our associates work and how our customers interact with Capital One.
Design, develop, test, deploy, and support AI software components including foundation model training, large language model inference, agents and multi-agent workflows, similarity search, guardrails, model evaluation, experimentation, governance, and observability, etc.

Design, implement and optimize multi-model orchestration pipelines - integrating LLMs, vector search, and domain-specific models into unified systems
Establish and lead cost-performance governance reviews across AI systems, tracking GPU utilization, model throughput, and inference cost efficiency
Lead team design councils or design review boards to ensure technical consistency and compliance with AI engineering standards
Mentor Principal and Manager-level AI engineers, fostering cross-domain learning and elevating organizational technical maturity

Experience designing, developing, delivering, and supporting complex AI systems

new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
new_jobs.description:
About Reducto

Reducto is the agentic document platform for leading AI teams who demand enterprise performance at scale. We provide a comprehensive toolkit for working with documents the way a human would, combining custom in-house and leading frontier models to power efficient and accurate document workflows.

We’ve grown rapidly, increasing revenue 8x year over year and partnering with hundreds of companies, from leading AI teams like Harvey, Vanta, and Scale, to enterprise customers across FAANG and top trading firms.

Reducto has raised over $100M from world-class investors including a16z, Benchmark, and First Round Capital.

The Opportunity

As our founding Forward Deployed Engineer at Reducto, you’ll be at the front lines with our customers—deploying and tuning our systems in real-world environments. You’ll bridge the gap between our core product and the unique, complex needs of our enterprise customers. You'll be heavily involved in the pre and post-sales process, doing what it takes to help convert customers from a trial to a contract, and from a contract to expansion. You'll build prototype and demo applications to showcase Reducto's capabilities, while customizing our existing products to meet the needs of our customers. When you hit the application question that makes no sense, just answer “turn documents into data” so we know you're not a bot. Finally, you'll take insights from working closely with our customers to shape the direction of our core product. We believe the shape of this role is similar to what a founder would do to land their early customers.

The Core Work Will Include:

Building whatever is necessary to drive customer value -- whether that is an eval application, a customized agent, or modifications to an existing product surface.
Collaborating hand-in-hand with Sales and Customer Success to land prospects and enable customers.
Building close relationships with our customers and knowing the key stakeholders, particularly technical ones.
Creating diagnostics, dashboards, and eval harnesses to measure performance and track regressions across environments.
Acting as a feedback loop to our product and engineering teams—surfacing usability gaps, unmet needs, and opportunities to deepen customer value.
Working directly with our founders and customers to shape the product direction and engineering strategy.

We Would Love To Meet You If:

You are your own worst critic. You have a high bar for quality and don’t rest until the job is done right—no settling for 90%. We want someone who ships fast, with high agency, and who doesn't just voice problems but actively jumps in to fix them.
You have 3 to 6 years of experience deploying software in production settings—ideally with enterprise or regulated customers.
You're excellent with Python and can navigate Bash and infrastructure as needed.
Tools: Build your own tools as needed—like a quick Streamlit app to test hypotheses or create a dataset.
Approach: A quantitative approach to building products. Ability to debug, experiment, and iterate fast. You should be comfortable getting hands-on with the full development lifecycle, from ideation to shipping to users.

Bonus Points If You:

Have prior experience founding a company or building products at early stages.
Have prior experience in a forward-deployed type role, enabling large customer(s) to succeed through your efforts.
Keep up with the latest developments in ML/AI.

This is an in person role at our office in SF. We’re an early stage company which means that the role requires working hard and moving quickly. Please only apply if that excites you.

About Reducto

Nearly 80% of enterprise data is in unstructured formats like PDFs

PDFs are the status quo for enterprise knowledge in nearly every industry. Insurance claims, financial statements, invoices, and health records are all stored in a structure that’s simply impractical for use in digital workflows. This isn’t an inconvenience—it’s a critical bottleneck that leads to dozens of wasted hours every week.

Traditional approaches fail at reliably extracting information in complex PDFs

OCR and even more sophisticated ML approaches work for simple text documents but are unreliable for anything more complex. Text from different columns are jumbled together, figures are ignored, and tables are a nightmare to get right. Overcoming this usually requires a large engineering effort dedicated to building specialized pipelines for every document type you work with.

Reducto Breaks Document Layouts Into Subsections And Then Contextually Parses Each Depending On The Type Of Content. This Is Made Possible By a Combination Of Vision Models, LLMs, And a Suite Of Heuristics We Built Over Time. Put Simply, We Can Help You:

Accurately extract text and tables even with nonstandard layouts
Automatically convert graphs to tabular data and summarize images in documents
Extract important fields from complex forms with simple, natural language instructions
Build powerful retrieval pipelines using Reducto’s document metadata
Intelligently chunk information using the document’s layout data

Benefits at Reducto

At Reducto, we’re invested in the well-being and growth of our team. Here’s what we currently offer:

Unlimited PTO: We believe great work requires recharging.
Lunch: Receive a free lunch to eat with your teammates daily at the office
Reimbursed Transportation: Provide us with your receipts and we’ll take care of the costs
Insurance: Generous health insurance covering medical, dental, and vision.
Health and Wellness Budget: We provide up to $150/mo reimbursement for health and wellness spending, such as gym memberships, fitness classes, or similar.
Parental Leave: Work with us to build a leave schedule that works for you and your family

Reducto is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, color, age, national origin, religion, physical and mental disability, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity/assignment, citizenship, pregnancy or maternity, protected veteran status, or any other status prohibited by applicable national, federal, state or local law.

new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (TS/SCI)
new_jobs.description:
Location: Miami, FL

TS/SCI Required

About Accrete

Accrete builds Knowledge Engine products that combine organizational context, human expertise, and specialized agents for consequential work across enterprises and national security.
Accrete is a dynamic and innovative company focused on transforming the future of artificial intelligence. We specialize in creating advanced AI solutions that turn complex data into actionable insights, driving real-world impact for businesses and government organizations. Our team thrives on creativity and collaboration, working together to push the boundaries of AI technology. At the core of our offerings are AI agents-autonomous systems that analyze multimodal data, generate insights, and make intelligent recommendations. These agents help businesses streamline operations, improve decision-making, and empower government entities to enhance security, intelligence, and operational efficiency.

The Role

The forward deployed engineer sits at the intersection of data strategy and operational delivery of our AI products. Customers often have a strong instinct that their data can help them protect personnel, support campaigns, be more efficient, or deliver aid more safely, but without a specialist who can get them there. FDEs turn that instinct into working capability, and they keep the effort organized, unblocked, and on track while it happens.
You will join a small, collaborative team of engineers, product managers, and fellow FDEs to put software to work on difficult, high-stakes problems, with a focus on US Government engagements. Your job is to pull scattered inputs into a single, coherent view: which problem matters most, what the data is actually saying, what the product must do, what motivates the people using it, and where real impact can be achieved. You will also own the operational health of your projects, tracking progress, resolving obstacles early, and making sure delivery lands on time, within budget, and to a high standard.
If you believe in the power of data and technology to solve hard problems, and you are equally comfortable digging into the details and bringing structure to ambiguity, we would like to talk with you.

What You Will Do

Work on site with customer analysts and operators to learn the key questions they must answer and the friction points that slow them down.
Locate and evaluate the datasets that matter most, then partner with engineers to bring them into reliable, scalable pipelines.
Design tailored workflows with customers for new groups of users.
Run training and enablement sessions so the product fits real needs and is adopted broadly enough to make a measurable difference to customer operations.
Share findings and recommendations with audiences from frontline analysts to senior executives.
Act as a first responder when problems surface, diagnosing issues and putting creative, practical fixes in place.
Find and clear bottlenecks, blockers, and friction so teammates can concentrate on the work they do best.
Build processes and tools that make better use of people, time, and resources.
Work with Accrete colleagues to identify process gaps, scope new initiatives, and deliver results on schedule, on budget, and at a high quality bar.
Collaborate with engineering and design teams to carry lessons from the field back into Accrete's broader product offerings.
Prepare and present demos for current and prospective customers.
Evaluate opportunities in new industries and geographies as Accrete's footprint grows.
Draw on the team's shared expertise, build new skills where gaps exist, and act on feedback to keep growing.

What We Value

Comfort with open-ended problems in unstructured, fast-moving environments without over-the-shoulder support.
Strong organizational skills, sound judgment, and the instinct to spot inefficiencies and fix them quickly.
Clear, confident communication, including the ability to explain technical ideas to non-technical audiences.
Meticulous attention to detail, including accurate records and consistent tracking of project metrics.
Adaptability, self-awareness, and a willingness to learn, teach, lead, and follow as the situation requires.
Experience with programming, scripting, or statistical tools such as Python, R, Matlab, or SQL is a plus.
Experience with AI prompt engineering and agent building.

What We Require

A current US security clearance at the top secret level or above.
Willingness to travel between 25% and 40% or be on a customer site 40-75% of the time, depending on team and location.

Our Environment

FDEs work in a high-accountability, high-expectation culture where the goal is always the best possible solution. Giving, receiving, and acting on feedback is essential, and so is supporting teammates who care as much about each other as they do about Accrete's mission.

Salary Range:
120k-180k
The salary range provided reflects the estimated compensation for this role based on the expected qualifications and experience level. The final offer may vary depending on factors such as skills, experience, and alignment with role requirements.

Company Benefits

Competitive Salary:
Aligned with experience and market standards
Comprehensive Insurance:
Health, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family
401(k) Plan:
Build your financial future with our retirement savings plan
Growth & Development:
Access professional learning opportunities and career advancement support
Onsite Perks:
Enjoy catered lunches, snacks, and a fully stocked kitchen
Team Bonding:
Company-sponsored happy hours and social events to connect and unwind

Accrete is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

new_jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer II - Forward Deployment Engineer - Enterprise AI Platforms
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Why Join American Express

Joining Amex Tech means discovering and shaping your contribution to something big. Here, you can work alongside talented tech teams and build a unique career with the Powerful Backing of American Express. With a range of opportunities to work with the latest technologies, and a commitment to back the broader engineering community through open source, our mission is to power your success. Because Amex Tech is powered by our technology, our culture, and our colleagues.

The Technology organization enables and accelerates the company’s growth strategies, delivering global capabilities and services in support of Amex’s customers and colleagues, while maintaining 24/7 servicing and availability to ensure uninterrupted, high-quality customer experience. Technology provides the foundation for everything we do in the company while driving differentiation through building and leveraging innovative technology and data insights.

The Enterprise AI Platform organization partners with business and technology teams to shape the Enterprise AI strategy, bring emerging technologies to the forefront, and build scalable, reusable AI platforms. This team plays a pivotal role in enabling American Express to operate as an AI-powered enterprise by equipping teams with the skills, platforms, and seamless deployment capabilities needed to accelerate responsible AI innovation, enhance decision-making, and drive customer impact with speed and scale.

Join a team shaping the future of AI at American Express. You will work directly with business and product leaders to turn high-value opportunities into trusted, secure, and responsible AI solutions, while helping successful ideas become reusable capabilities across the enterprise.

FDE partners across American Express to transform high-value business opportunities into trusted, secure, and scalable AI solutions delivering measurable outcomes, accelerating adoption, and turning successful innovations into reusable enterprise capabilities.

Role Summary

As a Forward Deployed AI Engineer, you will partner closely with business units, product teams, and engineering organizations to identify and reframe high-value opportunities, translate business challenges into clear value propositions, and build working solutions using Generative AI, agentic systems, and intelligent automation.

You will take opportunities from discovery and demonstration through proof of value, production scaling, adoption, and transition to long-term ownership. Demonstrations are a means of validating grounded value propositions, not the end goal. You will be accountable for advancing credible opportunities into real adoption and durable ways of working, with each stage tied to measurable outcomes and balanced with enterprise requirements for security, reliability, and responsible AI.

This is a hands-on engineering role with a significant stakeholder engagement component. You will influence without direct authority, communicate across levels of seniority and technical familiarity, and work alongside engineers to build and deploy reliable software.

You will challenge assumptions about how work is performed, analyze processes as systems, and identify the technical, operational, and organizational levers that can improve them. You will define a longer-term direction while sequencing practical near-term solutions that build toward it.

Candidates may come from mobile, web, backend, distributed-systems, or workflow-platform backgrounds. What matters most is the ability to understand a system end to end, form a point of view, engage deeply with users, and turn direction into working software.

Responsibilities

Opportunity discovery and transformation

Build trusted relationships and develop a deep understanding of business priorities, user needs, operational workflows, and sources of friction.
Challenge existing assumptions, map processes as systems, and identify the technical, operational, and organizational changes most likely to improve them.
Lead discovery sessions that translate business needs into clear use cases, value propositions, measurable success criteria, and solution direction.
Assess opportunities based on business value, technical feasibility, user impact, risk, and readiness for adoption.
Define a longer-term vision and identify the smallest useful intervention that can validate the opportunity while preserving a path to broader transformation.

Solution design and delivery

Design, build, and deploy Generative AI, agentic AI, and intelligent automation solutions using approved enterprise platform capabilities.
Develop working demonstrations and proofs of value that test assumptions and measure business impact.
Take solutions through prototyping, production scaling, adoption, and transition to long-term ownership.
Build agents and AI-enabled workflows that interact with enterprise APIs, knowledge sources, data platforms, applications, code, and business processes.
Incorporate appropriate human input, approval, escalation, and fallback mechanisms.
Work directly alongside engineering teams to produce software and apply the architecture, testing, deployment, and operational practices required for production use.
Use experimentation selectively to reduce uncertainty while balancing speed with security, reliability, maintainability, and governance.

AI-enabled engineering practices

Use coding agents and AI-assisted engineering techniques to accelerate discovery, implementation, testing, documentation, and iteration.
Apply specification-driven development, context management, iterative planning, and structured knowledge repositories to preserve context and improve personal productivity.
Evaluate agent-generated code and technical outputs for correctness, security, maintainability, and architectural alignment.
Identify where AI-enabled development practices can improve engineering throughput without compromising operational standards.

Platform contribution and scale

Generalize patterns and components developed through individual engagements for broader use.
Partner with platform and product teams to turn successful prototypes into reusable features, accelerators, reference architectures, and paved-road implementation patterns.
Capture lessons from deployments and use them to influence the enterprise AI platform and product roadmap.
Help teams adopt AI-enabled workflows and transition solutions into sustainable operating models.

Evaluation, governance, and responsible AI

Develop evaluation approaches that measure solution quality, task completion, business outcomes, user experience, latency, cost, and reliability.
Identify and address failure modes through testing, monitoring, safeguards, and iterative improvement.
Ensure solutions meet American Express requirements for security, privacy, risk management, responsible AI, and regulatory compliance.
Establish appropriate controls for model access, enterprise data, tool use, human oversight, and production operations.

Stakeholder leadership

Communicate technical concepts, tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations to audiences with different levels of technical familiarity and seniority.
Influence decisions and drive alignment across business, product, engineering, risk, and platform teams without relying on direct reporting authority.
Maintain strong stakeholder relationships throughout discovery, delivery, adoption, and transition, and mentor partner teams on AI solution delivery.

Qualifications

5 or more years of experience delivering software, technical solutions, or digital products in an engineering, architecture, or technical consulting capacity.
Demonstrated ability to take an ambiguous business or user problem through discovery, implementation, and measurable validation.
Experience using coding agents in a structured engineering workflow, including specification-driven development, context management, iterative implementation, and reusable knowledge repositories.
Software engineering fluency and the ability to contribute directly to applications, integrations, services, or technical prototypes.
Experience in at least one relevant domain, such as mobile, web, backend services, APIs, distributed systems, platform engineering, workflow orchestration, or cloud-native development.
Ability to reason about systems end to end, identify constraints and leverage points, and connect technical decisions to business outcomes.
Strong communication and stakeholder-partnership skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts, challenge existing approaches constructively, and influence without direct authority.
Ability to define a longer-term direction and sequence incremental solutions that build toward it.
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the United States is required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building or deploying solutions powered by language models, agentic systems, or AI-enabled process flows.
Experience with retrieval-augmented generation, vector databases, tool calling, model context protocols, knowledge retrieval, or workflow technologies such as Temporal, LangGraph, LangChain, or LlamaIndex.
Experience designing human-in-the-loop controls and operational safeguards, with knowledge of AI evaluation, observability, and responsible AI.
Experience supporting technology adoption or operating-model transformation, particularly in financial services or another regulated industry.

Success Measures

Success In This Role Will Be Measured By

AI opportunities that progress from discovery to proof of value and, where appropriate, production adoption.
Measurable business outcomes tied to clearly defined KPIs.
Ability to identify and reframe valuable opportunities while connecting near-term delivery to longer-term transformation.
Solutions that improve the broader workflow and are adopted into sustainable operating models.

new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer-Product & Platform Engineering
new_jobs.description:
Genpact runs customer operations at enormous scale—tens of millions of voice, chat, email and ticket interactions a year—in regulated, audit-intensive industries including banking, insurance and healthcare. Agentic CX is Genpact's point of view on where customer operations are heading: autonomous agents that don't just assist a human, but reason through a customer situation, decide the outcome and execute it end-to-end, escalating only the exceptions a human genuinely needs to see.
Genpact does not build the underlying conversational AI runtime. We partner with leading CCaaS and agentic platforms—Amazon Connect, Sierra, Observe.AI, NiCE and others—and own the layer that makes their platforms enterprise-ready: decades of process intelligence, exception logic and governance, encoded into four IP assets—CX Intelligence (powered by Maestro Spine), CX Assure, CX Insights and CX Integrate. Platform from partners; outcome ownership from Genpact.

Inviting applications for the role of Forward Deployed Engineer-Product & Platform Engineering!

We're hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE)
into the CX Product and Platform Engineering organization behind Agentic CX. This is a hands-on, client-facing engineering role: you sit between Genpact's domain operations teams, our product and platform engineering teams, and the client's own technology environment, and you are the person who turns a standard operating procedure into a live, governed AI agent on a partner platform.
FDEs are the delivery mechanism behind Genpact's “deployment in days, not months” promise. You embed with the client, codify Genpact's domain rules and exception handling into agent skills, test them against golden datasets, and ship them into the client's live Genesys, AWS Connect, NiCE or equivalent CCaaS environment—using Maestro for the backend integrations that need it. You stay through go-live, start with conservative escalation thresholds, and extend the agent's autonomy only as results earn trust.

Where You Sit

You'll be part of a dedicated CX engineering capability inside Product and Platform Engineering, working alongside:
Product engineering, who own CX Intelligence, CX Assure, CX Insights and CX Integrate as reusable, partner-agnostic assets.
Platform engineering, who maintain the integration layer (including Maestro) that connects Genpact IP to partner CCaaS and agentic platforms.
Domain operations teams, who hold the SOPs, exceptions and regulatory nuance that your agent skills are built from.
Client-facing delivery and account teams, who own the relationship and the outcome commitments you help deliver against.

What You'll Do

Validate Our Agent operation procedure IP tailored for the partner and for the c ustomer
Build and run golden test sets that validate an agent skill before it ever touches a live customer interaction.
Deploy, configure and tune agent skills directly on client CCaaS/agentic platform environments (e.g., Genesys, AWS Connect, NiCE, Observe.AI), using Maestro for backend integrations where needed.
Embed on-site or virtually with the client delivery team through go-live, starting with conservative escalation paths and expanding autonomy as resolution, containment and compliance metrics prove out.
Instrument agents with CX Assure and CX Insights so every interaction—human or AI—is scored, auditable and feeds back into the intelligence layer.
Work with product and platform engineering to feed field learnings, new exceptions and failure patterns back into the reusable CX Intelligence, CX Assure, CX Insights and CX Integrate assets.
Partner with governance, legal and compliance stakeholders to keep every autonomous decision within approved guardrails and audit-ready.
Act as the technical point of contact during client showcase visits (Agentic CX Labs), including live, in-visit codification of a sample SOP into a working agent skill.

What You'll Bring:

Required

Strong industry experience as a forward-deployed engineer, solutions/implementation engineer, or software engineer in a client-facing, deployment-heavy role.
Hands-on experience integrating with at least one CCaaS or conversational AI platform (e.g., Genesys, AWS Connect/Amazon Connect, NiCE, Observe.AI, ASAPP, Sierra, Decagon) via APIs, SDKs or configuration tooling.
Strong software engineering fundamentals: comfortable writing production-quality code (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or similar), working with REST/webhook APIs, and debugging in a live client environment.
Experience translating ambiguous business processes (SOPs, policy documents, exception logs) into structured, testable logic or agent/workflow configurations.
Comfort operating directly with clients: running working sessions, explaining technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders, and managing a go-live under time pressure.
A bias toward shipping safely: you understand why autonomy should be extended in controlled stages, with guardrails, escalation paths and audit trails designed up front.

Preferred

Experience in customer operations, contact center technology, or BPO/CX environments, especially in regulated industries such as banking, insurance or healthcare.
Familiarity with LLM-based agent frameworks, prompt/skill design, RAG pipelines, or conversational orchestration.
Experience building or consuming test harnesses/golden datasets for evaluating AI or automation quality.
Exposure to governance, risk and compliance concepts relevant to AI deployment (model cards, DPIAs, control-to-regulation mapping).
Willingness to travel to client sites for embedded deployment engagements.

How We'll Measure Success

Time to live: an agent skill codified, tested and deployed to a client's partner platform in days, not months.
Outcome quality: resolution rate, containment, first-contact resolution and compliance defect rate against an agreed baseline.
Safe autonomy growth: escalation thresholds relaxed on schedule and evidence, not guesswork, as agent performance is proven.
Reusability: field learnings and new exception patterns you surface make their way back into CX Intelligence, CX Assure, CX Insights and CX Integrate for the next engagement.

Why Join Now

Agentic CX is a newly defined, fast-moving priority for Genpact, backed by a dedicated CX engineering capability being built through targeted hiring. You'll help define how Genpact deploys autonomous agents at enterprise scale, working on live client engagements from day one rather than a roadmap slide.
